For urban freeways on weekdays, both FleetDNA and CE-CERT peak before the first MOVES3 peak and do not display the bimodal distribution that is characteristic of MOVES3 weekday defaults. For urban other roads on weekends, both FleetDNA and CE- CERT drive more in the morning and less in the evening compared to the MOVES3 distribution, but CE-CERT’s highest fraction matches more closely in hour ID to MOVES3 than FleetDNA, which peaks even earlier in the morning. On urban other roads on weekdays, CE-CERT interestingly matches more closely to the bimodal distribution of MOVES3 but contrasts MOVES3 with a higher morning peak than evening, following the general trend of more hours driven in the morning for commercial data sets compared to MOVES defaults. Interestingly, on urban freeways on weekdays, the first peak in the CE-CERT distribution neatly aligns with MOVES3 defaults; however, CE-CERT drives more miles before this peak and less after compared to MOVES3, similar to FleetDNA’s trend for this group. Urban freeways on weekends have the unique distinction of driving more miles than MOVES3 in the late evening, but data are not robust for this category. Urban other roads on weekends see less driving in the evening hours from CE-CERT, as does FleetDNA. Also like FleetDNA, the distribution peaks just after the morning peak of MOVES3, but FleetDNA trucks drove more at midday than in the morning compared to CE-CERT for urban other roads on weekdays.
